No confirmed devices were discovered. Listen to this article with a free profile00:0000:00An SAS aircraft flying from Copenhagen lands, after receiving a bomb threat, at Warsaw Chopin Airport in Poland on Tuesday.Piotr Bozyk / via ReutersShareAdd NBC News to GoogleNov. 3, 2026, 10:16 AM EST / Source: ReutersBy ReutersAt least four flights in Europe were subjected to bomb threats on Tuesday after one on Monday, forcing some to divert and an airport in Poland to briefly close, although no confirmed devices were discovered.

Authorities diverted a LOT flight from London that was meant to land at Warsaw’s Chopin airport to another nearby airport, Modlin, which was briefly closed while the plane was searched. Modlin airport said it had reopened after no device was found.

Another Warsaw-bound flight, an SAS flight from Copenhagen, landed at Chopin as scheduled. Chopin airport said no device was found and the airport remained operational.

Counter-terrorism units were checking the plane for possible explosive devices, BTA news agency quoted Interior Ministry Secretary General Lyubomir Nikolov as saying.

Parts of an airport in Murcia, in southeastern Spain, were cordoned off on Tuesday after a bomb threat was reported on a Ryanair flight from Manchester. But officials said the report proved to be a hoax, and the airport resumed normal operations after authorities found no explosives on board.
